title: KT docs vs Devin Wiki
lede: On three open-source repositories, NeoDevEx's KT engine now answers repository questions about as well as Devin (79.7% vs 70.3%, or 78.3% if Devin gets credit for answering from newer code) and makes a false claim in 4% of answers against Devin's 21%. Reading the generated docs alone, the two are even (51.3% vs 52.3%). Devin's wiki still covers more of each codebase. Before this study our docs scored 36.3%; every gap we found is listed below with the fix and the re-measured result.

modeNotes.wiki: Reading the docs: a neutral reader model (Gemini 2.5 Flash, temperature 0, the same prompt for both) answers each question using only the generated wiki. This measures how much a new engineer can learn from the docs alone.
modeNotes.ask: Asking the repo: each product's own question-answering over the repository. Devin through Ask Devin (DeepWiki MCP), NeoDevEx through the KT service's /chat/completions endpoint.

gaps.title: The docs covered too little of each codebase
gaps.finding: Our wikis had 9 to 11 pages and cited 19 to 33 files per repository; Devin's had 35 to 46 pages and cited 55 to 183. A reader of our docs found no answer to 26 of the 75 questions, against 2 for Devin.
gaps.fix: Page count now scales with the repository's file count instead of a flat 8 to 12. A deterministic coverage pass attaches every source file no page claimed to the page documenting the same module, and groups the rest into module reference pages.
gaps.effect: Pages 30 → 74. Files cited 78 → 214. Uncovered questions 26 → 7. Docs accuracy 36.3% → 51.3%. Devin still leads on breadth: 118 pages, 339 files, 2 uncovered.

gaps.title: The index skipped the files that answer workflow questions
gaps.finding: pyproject.toml was excluded by name, .toml, .mjs and .mts files were never indexed, build/ and bin/ were skipped even when they hold real source (hono's build script), and exclusions matched every folder in the absolute path, so a repo under a folder named tmp or build lost all of its files.
gaps.fix: Files tracked by git are treated as source. Manifests, CI workflows and tool configs are indexed. Exclusions match the repo-relative path only.
gaps.effect: hono indexed files 409 → 452. Dev-workflow questions: docs 8% → 42%, Q&A 44% → 75%.

gaps.title: Repository Q&A answered from fragments and from memory
gaps.finding: Answers were built from 350-word retrieved fragments, so the model filled the gaps from what it remembered about Flask or Hono: Python 3.8 support, DEBUG defaulting to None, invented fetch calls. 29% of answers contained a false claim.
gaps.fix: A cheap planning step picks the files the question needs from the file tree; those and the most-retrieved files are given in full with line numbers. The prompt now says the checked-out code overrides memory and every claim needs a file:line citation.
gaps.effect: Q&A accuracy 63.7% → 79.7%. Answers with a false claim 29.3% → 4.0%. Measured cost $0.12 per answer.

gaps.title: A third of our diagrams did not render
gaps.finding: 28 of 77 Mermaid diagrams failed to parse, almost all from unquoted labels containing parentheses and from unbalanced activation markers in sequence diagrams. Devin's failed 8% of the time.
gaps.fix: A deterministic sanitizer quotes such labels and removes unbalanced activations before any LLM repair. It was checked against Devin's 417 diagrams to make sure it never breaks a valid one.

gaps.title: Docs could describe a different commit than they claimed
gaps.finding: When cloning from GitHub the service always took the latest commit, even when asked for a specific one, and every source link pointed at HEAD, so links drifted as the repository changed.
gaps.fix: The clone is checked out at the requested commit, an index built from another commit is rebuilt, and links point at the commit.
gaps.effect: Links pinned to the documented commit 0 → 1,282 of 1,282.

gaps.title: Cost was not measured
gaps.finding: The KT service tracked no tokens or spend. The first meter we added also missed Gemini's thinking tokens, which the legacy SDK does not report separately.
gaps.fix: Every generation and answer is metered from provider-reported usage, including thinking tokens derived from the total, and priced at list price. Unknown models are flagged, never counted as free.
gaps.effect: Measured: $2.17 and 6.5 minutes per wiki on average, $0.12 per answer.

gaps.title: A dropped model stream could be published as documentation
gaps.finding: When the Gemini stream broke mid-page, the error text was saved as the page's content. One page in the after-fixes run was affected before the fix landed.
gaps.fix: Wiki generation now raises on a stream error so the page is retried; interactive chat still shows the error to the user.
gaps.effect: Covered by two regression tests. That one affected page (ky: test module reference) is left in the published data as found.

gaps.title: Different local repositories could share one index
gaps.finding: Local repositories were indexed under their folder name, and every agent workspace defaults to a folder called project.
gaps.fix: Local repositories are keyed by folder name plus a hash of the absolute path.

gaps.title: No way to ask the docs a question
gaps.finding: Devin shows an Ask box on every wiki. Our KT pages had none, although the service could already answer.
gaps.fix: KT repository pages now have an Ask panel that answers from the code at the documented commit, with file and line references.
gaps.effect: Shipped in the KT UI with tests.

method: Three public repositories of different shapes: a small TypeScript library, a mid-size Python framework and a large multi-runtime TypeScript framework.

NeoDevEx was pinned to the commit Devin's wiki was built from. ky shows its exact commit; for flask and hono, which show only a date, we used the last commit on main on or before that date (marked *).

75 questions (25 per repo) were written by reading only the source code at the pinned commit, before either wiki was opened. Each has a verified answer, atomic key facts and file:line evidence. Mix per repo: 5 architecture, 8 precise behaviour, 4 where-is-it, 4 edge cases, 4 dev workflow.

Answers were shuffled and labelled X / Y per question. Two independent graders scored every answer without knowing which tool wrote it, checking disputed claims against the code. A question scores 1 for correct, 0.5 for partly right, 0 otherwise, averaged across the two graders.

Citations were checked two ways: every citation mechanically (the file exists at the commit and the line range is inside it), and a random sample of up to 40 inline citations per wiki by a blind grader reading the cited lines.

Diagrams were parsed with mermaid 11. Cost comes from provider-reported token counts priced at Gemini list prices; NeoDevEx ran Gemini 2.5 Pro for pages and answers and Gemini 2.5 Flash for file planning.
caveats: The after-fixes numbers were measured on the same 75 questions that exposed the gaps. The fixes are general (coverage, indexing, retrieval, rendering) and none targets a specific question, but a held-out repository would be a stronger test; it is the first thing we will run next.

Devin's wiki for flask and hono shows only an index date, so those two commits are the last commit on or before that date. Line drift may explain part of Devin's unsupported citations there. On ky, where the commit matches exactly, 38% of Devin's sampled inline citations did not support their claim.
Devin's Ask answers from newer code than its wiki shows: 10 of its hono answers graded wrong are correct for hono's latest commit. The scorecard shows Devin's Q&A both ways.
Graders were two independent AI agents with repository access, not humans. They agreed on 95.8% of 600 verdicts.
The neutral reader for the docs test is Gemini 2.5 Flash, from the same model family NeoDevEx generates with.

Devin does not publish per-wiki cost or generation time. Its public DeepWiki is free to read; private repositories need a paid plan. Our times come from three repositories generating at once with four pages in parallel each.
Baseline generation cost is not compared because the baseline meter missed thinking tokens.

ky.question: How does a call like `ky.get(url, opts)` get from the public entry point to an actual fetch? Name the functions/classes involved.
ky.reference: source/index.ts createInstance() builds the `ky` function and per-method shortcuts; each merges instance defaults with call options via validateAndMerge() and calls the static Ky.create(input, options). Ky.create runs init hooks, constructs a Ky instance (which normalizes options and builds a Request), then an async pipeline runs beforeRequest hooks, #retry(() => #fetch()), afterResponse hooks, HTTPError/retry handling, and returns a ResponsePromise decorated with body shortcuts.

neodevex.note: Ky.create, constructor, beforeRequest, #retry/#fetch; no createInstance/validateAndMerge. / Ky.create/#retry/#fetch right; falsely says ky.get calls main ky() function.

devin.note: validateAndMerge, Ky.create, #retry/#fetch, timeout; no createInstance, hooks, ResponsePromise. / validateAndMerge, Ky.create, #retry, #fetch, timeout; omits createInstance, hooks, ResponsePromise.

ky.question: How do `ky.create()` and `ky.extend()` differ in how they treat the parent instance's defaults?
ky.reference: `create(newDefaults)` builds a fresh instance from only newDefaults (validateAndMerge(newDefaults)), ignoring the parent; `extend(newDefaults)` merges parent defaults with newDefaults (validateAndMerge(defaults, newDefaults)), and also accepts a function receiving the parent defaults.

neodevex.note: create vs extend right; omits function form of extend. / create ignores, extend merges; omits function form.

devin.note: create vs extend right; omits function form of extend. / create ignores, extend merges; omits function form.

ky.question: Describe the order in which hook types run during a request lifecycle that ends in a retried HTTP error and eventual failure.
ky.reference: init (synchronous, in Ky.create before the Ky constructor) -> beforeRequest (once, retryCount 0) -> fetch -> afterResponse (runs before the throwHttpErrors check) -> HTTPError built and data populated -> beforeRetry (before each retry, after the delay) -> fetch -> afterResponse ... -> when retries are exhausted, beforeError hooks run on the final error before it is thrown.

neodevex.note: Correct order; beforeError only at final failure. / init, single beforeRequest, afterResponse, beforeRetry, final beforeError.

devin.note: beforeError after each attempt and beforeRequest rerun on retry; both false. / Claims beforeError after first error and beforeRequest before retry.

ky.question: How does Ky combine a user-provided AbortSignal with its own timeout cancellation?
ky.reference: If AbortController and AbortSignal.any exist, the constructor stores the user signal (options.signal or the input Request's signal), creates an internal AbortController, and sets options.signal = AbortSignal.any([userSignal, internal.signal]) (or just the internal signal). The timeout() helper aborts the internal controller; on the next attempt #fetch replaces an aborted controller and recreates the Request with a new managed signal. Retry delays listen only to the user signal.

neodevex.note: Timeout abort right; wrongly says timeout signals are combined in merge.ts. / TimeoutError via controller right; falsely says merge collects internal timeout/totalTimeout signals.

devin.note: AbortSignal.any correct; misapplies merge.ts last-signal fallback to timeout combining. / AbortSignal.any combination; cites merge path; omits timeout abort/recreation/delay.

ky.question: How do Ky-specific options get separated from options passed through to the underlying fetch call?
ky.reference: In #fetch, findUnknownOptions(this.#options) (source/utils/options.ts) collects every own key that is in neither requestOptionsRegistry (standard RequestInit keys already applied to the Request) nor kyOptionKeys (Ky's own options), and passes that object as fetch's second argument. This forwards fetch-only extensions like `dispatcher`, `priority`, or Next.js `next`.

neodevex.note: Claims NormalizedOptions go to fetch; misses findUnknownOptions passthrough. / Claims NormalizedOptions are passed to fetch; misses findUnknownOptions.

devin.note: Registries and unknown-option passthrough in options.ts. / Registries and unknown-key passthrough in options.ts.

ky.question: What are the default retry settings (limit, methods, status codes, afterStatusCodes, delay formula)?
ky.reference: limit 2; methods get, put, head, delete, options, trace; statusCodes 408, 413, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504; afterStatusCodes 413, 429, 503; maxRetryAfter and backoffLimit Infinity; delay = 0.3 * 2^(attemptCount-1) * 1000 ms (300, 600, ...); jitter undefined; retryOnTimeout false.

neodevex.note: All defaults correct.

devin.note: All defaults correct.

ky.question: What is the default per-attempt `timeout`, the default `totalTimeout`, and what happens if timeout exceeds the max?
ky.reference: timeout defaults to 10000 ms per attempt; totalTimeout defaults to false (disabled). If either is a number greater than 2147483647, the request promise rejects with a RangeError.

neodevex.note: Both defaults right; RangeError behavior not known. / timeout and totalTimeout right; RangeError not covered.

devin.note: timeout default and RangeError; totalTimeout default unknown. / timeout and RangeError right; totalTimeout not covered.

ky.question: When is a timed-out request retried by default, and what error type is thrown on timeout?
ky.reference: A timeout throws TimeoutError (extends KyError). By default it is NOT retried because retryOnTimeout is false; it is retried only if retry.retryOnTimeout is true or a shouldRetry function returns true.

neodevex.note: Not retried, TimeoutError; omits shouldRetry override. / Not retried by default, TimeoutError; omits shouldRetry.

devin.note: Not retried, TimeoutError; omits shouldRetry override. / TimeoutError, retryOnTimeout false; omits shouldRetry.

ky.question: In what order are checks performed when deciding whether to retry a non-forced error?
ky.reference: #calculateRetryDelay: (1) if retryCount >= limit, throw; (2) ForceRetryError short-circuits with custom/computed delay; (3) if request method not in retry.methods, throw; (4) user shouldRetry: false -> throw, true -> retry, other -> fall through; (5) TimeoutError retried only if retryOnTimeout; (6) HTTPError retried only if status in statusCodes, honoring Retry-After for afterStatusCodes; (7) otherwise only NetworkError is retried, all other errors thrown.

neodevex.note: Correct order incl. shouldRetry semantics and NetworkError. / Order and shouldRetry semantics right; no ForceRetry; 413 simplified.

devin.note: Top order right; 413 check placed before Retry-After handling, omits network errors. / Top order right; wrongly puts 413 check before afterStatusCodes/Retry-After; no ForceRetry.

ky.question: Which response headers does Ky consult for the retry delay, in what order, and how is a numeric value interpreted?
ky.reference: For statuses in afterStatusCodes it checks Retry-After, then RateLimit-Reset, X-RateLimit-Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Reset, X-Rate-Limit-Reset. A numeric value is seconds (multiplied by 1000); if that product is >= Date.parse('2024-01-01') it is treated as an epoch timestamp and Date.now() is subtracted. Non-numeric values are parsed as HTTP dates. The result is clamped at >= 0 and capped by maxRetryAfter, with no jitter applied.

neodevex.note: Only Retry-After named; seconds, cap, no jitter right.

devin.note: Header order right; omits date parsing and cap. / Header order and seconds/threshold right; omits date parse and cap.

ky.question: What is the exact message format of an HTTPError, and what is `error.data`?
ky.reference: Message: `Request failed with status code <status> <statusText>: <METHOD> <url>` (falls back to 'an unknown error' if no status). error.data is the pre-read response body: parsed JSON (via parseJson or JSON.parse) when Content-Type is a JSON subtype, otherwise text; undefined if empty, parse failure, over 10 MiB, or the read times out.

neodevex.note: Format and data semantics correct. / Exact format and data semantics.

devin.note: Message format NOT COVERED; data description mostly right. / Message not covered; data JSON/text and 10 MiB right.

ky.question: What does the `.json()` shortcut on the response promise do with headers and with an empty body?
ky.reference: It sets the Accept header to 'application/json' unless an Accept header is already set (the fetch is deferred by `await Promise.resolve()` so this happens first). On an empty body without a schema it calls JSON.parse('') which throws a SyntaxError; with a schema it validates `undefined`. A schema failure throws SchemaValidationError.

neodevex.note: Accept header right; empty-body behavior not covered. / Accept header right; empty body not covered.

devin.note: Claims empty body returns empty string; it throws. / Accept right; claims empty body returns empty string (actually throws).

ky.question: How is the final error passed through `beforeError` hooks, and which errors bypass them?
ky.reference: Each beforeError hook is awaited in order with {request, options, error, retryCount}; if a hook returns an Error instance it replaces the error for subsequent hooks and the final throw, otherwise the previous error is kept. Non-Error thrown values and errors thrown by beforeRetry hooks bypass beforeError entirely. init hook errors are synchronous and not caught either.

neodevex.note: Replacement semantics right; misses beforeRetry and non-Error bypasses. / Sequential replace right; SchemaValidationError bypass true; omits non-Error/beforeRetry.

devin.note: Claims Timeout/Network/ForceRetry errors bypass beforeError; false. / Falsely says Timeout/Network/ForceRetry errors bypass beforeError and #retry catches it.

ky.question: Where is network-error detection implemented and how does it decide something is a network error?
ky.reference: source/utils/is-network-error.ts, isRawNetworkError() (inlined from is-network-error v1.3.1). It requires a TypeError and matches runtime-specific messages (e.g. 'Failed to fetch', 'fetch failed', 'terminated', 'NetworkError when attempting to fetch resource.', Deno 'error sending request for url', Safari 'Load failed' with no stack). Ky#fetch wraps matches in NetworkError with the original as cause.

neodevex.note: NetworkError wrapping in Ky.ts; omits is-network-error.ts logic. / NetworkError wrap in Ky.ts right; no isRawNetworkError or heuristics.

devin.note: Right file; wrongly says checks error.cause messages, omits TypeError rule. / File right; falsely says checks error cause; omits TypeError/NetworkError wrap.

ky.question: Where is the per-attempt timeout implemented?
ky.reference: source/utils/timeout.ts default export timeout(request, init, abortController, options): a Promise wrapper (Promise.race workaround) that sets a setTimeout to abort the controller and reject with TimeoutError, clearing it when fetch settles. It is called from Ky#fetch with effectiveTimeout = min(timeout, remaining totalTimeout).

neodevex.note: Right file/function only. / timeout.ts location only.

devin.note: Right file and race; omits TimeoutError/abort and call site. / timeout.ts and race right; no TimeoutError or totalTimeout cap.

ky.question: Where is the deep-merging of options (headers, hooks, searchParams, context, signal) for extend/instances implemented?
ky.reference: source/utils/merge.ts: validateAndMerge() validates sources then calls deepMerge(); deepMerge special-cases signal (combined via AbortSignal.any), context (shallow merge), searchParams (appendSearchParameters), hooks (mergeHooks, concatenating arrays), and headers (mergeHeaderContainers/mergeHeaders). replaceOption() marks a value to replace instead of merge.

neodevex.note: deepMerge in merge.ts; no specifics or validateAndMerge. / deepMerge in merge.ts only.

devin.note: deepMerge/validateAndMerge and helpers; omits replaceOption. / validateAndMerge/deepMerge, hooks, context, signal; no replaceOption; line ranges off.

ky.question: Where are upload and download progress implemented?
ky.reference: source/utils/body.ts: streamResponse() (download, used in Ky.create when onDownloadProgress is set) and streamRequest() (upload, used by Ky#wrapRequestWithUploadProgress), both piping through withProgress() TransformStream; getBodySize() estimates upload size. Progress reports percent capped below 1 until the stream flushes.

neodevex.note: Functions and withProgress; omits getBodySize. / body.ts functions and withProgress; no getBodySize.

devin.note: streamRequest/streamResponse in body.ts; no withProgress/getBodySize.

ky.question: A POST request gets a 503. Does Ky retry it by default?
ky.reference: No. 'post' is not in the default retry.methods (get, put, head, delete, options, trace), so the method check throws the HTTPError without retrying, even though 503 is a retriable status.

neodevex.note: POST not in methods; method checked first.

devin.note: POST not in default methods.

ky.question: A GET receives 413 without any Retry-After-style header. Is it retried?
ky.reference: No. 413 is in statusCodes, but without a retry-after header Ky explicitly throws for 413; it is only retried when a Retry-After (or equivalent) header is present, since 413 is also in afterStatusCodes.

neodevex.note: Answer no, but claims 413 is never retried; retried with Retry-After. / Correct 'No' but claims 413 is never retried (retried with header).

devin.note: Not retried without header. / Not retried without header; throw path described.

ky.question: With `retry: 2` (default limit), how many total HTTP attempts can happen, and does `retry: {limit: 0}` change body handling?
ky.reference: Up to 3 attempts (1 initial + 2 retries), since retry stops when retryCount >= limit. With limit 0, Ky skips request.clone() before fetching, avoiding ReadableStream tee() buffering of streaming bodies.

neodevex.note: 3 attempts right; body cloning not covered.

devin.note: 3 attempts right; body cloning not covered. / 3 attempts right; misses clone/tee skip.

ky.question: If a beforeRequest hook returns a Response with status 500, will Ky retry it?
ky.reference: No. Ky skips fetch and the retry loop; because the response came from a hook (responseFromHook), a non-OK response still goes through afterResponse hooks and then throws HTTPError immediately without retrying (same for a Response returned from beforeRetry).

neodevex.note: No retry, goes to afterResponse; omits HTTPError thrown. / No retry, skips fetch; HTTPError throw not stated.

devin.note: No retry right; wrongly says Response returned as success. / No retry right; falsely says 500 Response returned as success.

flask.question: Trace the call chain when a WSGI server calls a Flask app for one request, from Flask.__call__ to the view function.
flask.reference: Flask.__call__ calls wsgi_app, which creates an AppContext with request_context(environ) and pushes it. It then calls full_dispatch_request(ctx). That sends request_started, runs preprocess_request (url_value_preprocessors, then before_request funcs), then dispatch_request (raises any stored routing exception, answers automatic OPTIONS, otherwise calls view_functions[rule.endpoint](**view_args) through ensure_sync). Any exception goes to handle_user_exception. finalize_request then runs make_response and process_response and sends request_finished. If an exception escapes, wsgi_app calls handle_exception. Finally it calls ctx.pop(error).

neodevex.note: wsgi_app, push, full_dispatch, dispatch; omits finalize, handle_exception, pop. / Covers call/wsgi_app/push/dispatch; omits finalize, handle_exception, ctx.pop.

devin.note: Chain through push/match/dispatch; omits finalize, error handling, pop. / Chain to view correct incl. push/match; omits finalize, exceptions, pop.

flask.question: What happens when a request context is pushed and popped in this checkout, and how are nested pushes handled?
flask.reference: There is one AppContext class; a request context is just an AppContext that has a request. push() bumps _push_count. If the context is already active it returns there. Otherwise it sets the _cv_app ContextVar, sends appcontext_pushed, and, if it has a request, opens the session via _get_session() and then runs match_request() for URL routing. pop() checks that the context is the active one and decrements the count. Cleanup only runs when the count reaches 0, in this order: do_teardown_request, request.close(), do_teardown_appcontext, reset the ContextVar, send appcontext_popped. Errors from these steps are collected and raised together at the end.

neodevex.note: Push count and nested handling right; pop order incomplete. / Push count, session before routing correct; pop order detail incomplete.

devin.note: Merged class and ContextVar; no push count or pop order. / Merged class and teardown mentioned; misses push counting and pop order.

flask.question: Walk through what app.register_blueprint(bp, **options) does internally.
flask.reference: App.register_blueprint (a setupmethod) calls blueprint.register(app, options). Blueprint.register works out the dotted name from name_prefix and the name option, and raises ValueError if that name is already in app.blueprints. It stores the blueprint in app.blueprints[name] and builds a BlueprintSetupState with make_setup_state. It adds the blueprint's static route if it has one. On first registration of the blueprint or the name, it merges the blueprint's handler dicts into the app with keys prefixed by the blueprint name (_merge_blueprint_funcs). It then replays every deferred_functions callback, recorded by record() from things like add_url_rule, against the state. Next it attaches CLI commands. Last, it recursively registers nested blueprints, joining url_prefix/subdomain and passing name_prefix=name.

neodevex.note: Setup state, deferred replay, nesting; omits duplicate-name ValueError. / Deferred replay, prefixes, nested recursion; misses duplicate-name ValueError.

devin.note: Deferred replay right; claims blueprints stored last (stored first); no ValueError/nesting. / Setup state and deferred replay; misses ValueError and nested recursion.

flask.question: How is the code split between src/flask/sansio/ and the top-level modules, and which classes collaborate?
flask.reference: The sansio package holds framework logic with no WSGI or I/O: sansio/scaffold.py defines Scaffold (route and handler registration dicts plus decorators), sansio/app.py defines App(Scaffold) (config, url_map, add_url_rule, error-handler lookup, redirect, register_blueprint), and sansio/blueprints.py defines Blueprint(Scaffold) and BlueprintSetupState. hono.question: Trace a request through Hono: what happens between app.fetch(request) and the returned Response?
hono.reference: app.fetch(request, env, ctx) calls the private HonoBase#dispatch(request, executionCtx, env, method). #dispatch computes the path with this.getPath, calls this.router.match(method, path), and builds a new Context holding the match result, env, executionCtx and the app's notFound handler. If exactly one handler matched, it is called directly with no compose, and its result (or the notFound handler's result) is returned. Otherwise compose(matchResult[0], errorHandler, notFoundHandler) runs the chain, and if the context is not finalized at the end it throws 'Context is not finalized. Did you forget to return a Response object or `await next()`?'. That error, like any other thrown Error, goes to the error handler.

The Cloudflare Pages handle passes eventContext.request, {...eventContext.env, eventContext} as env, and an executionCtx built from waitUntil and passThroughOnException. The AWS Lambda handle picks an EventProcessor for the event type (API Gateway v1/v2, ALB, Lattice) to build a Request. It calls app.fetch(req, {event, requestContext, lambdaContext}) and converts the Response back with processor.createResult, base64-encoding binary bodies. Request-conversion errors return 400 for a TypeError and 500 otherwise.

Calling add() after that first match throws 'Can not add a route since the matcher is already built.'

When the chain runs out and the context is not finalized, onNotFound runs. A returned response is assigned only when the context is not finalized yet or the response came from onError.

hono.question: How does bodyLimit() enforce the limit, and what is its default response?
hono.reference: maxSize is required and has no default. Requests without a body (for example GET or HEAD) go straight to next(). If Content-Length is present and Transfer-Encoding is not, the header is trusted: a value over maxSize calls onError, and otherwise next() runs. Otherwise (chunked, or no length header) the middleware reads the whole body up front, counting bytes and failing as soon as the size exceeds maxSize. It then rebuilds c.req.raw from the buffered chunks. The default onError throws HTTPException(413) wrapping a Response 'Payload Too Large' with status 413.

hono.question: What do the default notFound and error handlers return, and how are HTTPExceptions handled?
hono.reference: The default notFound handler returns c.text('404 Not Found', 404). The default error handler checks 'getResponse' in err, which is duck typing rather than an instanceof HTTPException check. If present, it returns c.newResponse(res.body, res) from err.getResponse(). Otherwise it calls console.error(err) and returns c.text('Internal Server Error', 500). app.onError() and app.notFound() replace these handlers. A thrown value that is not an Error is rethrown by #handleError instead of being handled.

hono.question: What are the defaults of c.redirect(), c.text(), c.json() and c.notFound()?
hono.reference: c.redirect(location, status?) sets the Location header and returns a response with status 302 by default. A location containing characters outside \x00-\xFF is passed through encodeURI. c.text() takes a fast path, returning new Response(text), when no headers, status, arguments or finalization exist. Otherwise it sets Content-Type 'text/plain; charset=UTF-8'. c.json() JSON.stringifies the value with Content-Type 'application/json'. c.notFound() calls the notFound handler the app passed into the Context, so a custom app.notFound applies. It falls back to an empty Response if none was passed.

hono.question: Where is the URL path extracted from a request, and where is the strict / non-strict trailing-slash behavior selected?

The choice is made in the HonoBase constructor: this.getPath = (strict ?? true) ? (options.getPath ?? getPath) : getPathNoStrict.

hono.question: Where does RegExpRouter build its matchers, and when does that happen?
hono.reference: In src/router/reg-exp-router/matcher.ts, function match(). On the first call it runs this.buildAllMatchers(), which RegExpRouter defines in router.ts and which builds one matcher per method from #routes and #middleware. It then replaces this.match with a closure that checks a static-path map first and otherwise runs one combined RegExp, using the index of the empty capture group to pick the handler set. hono.question: Where is request-body caching implemented, so that c.req.json() and c.req.text() can both be called?
hono.reference: In src/request.ts on the HonoRequest class: the public bodyCache field and the private #cachedBody(key) method. #cachedBody returns the cached promise for the same key. If a different body type was cached, it rebuilds the body from that cached value with new Response(body)[key](), stringifying first if the cached key was 'json'. Otherwise it reads raw[key]() and stores the promise. json() is implemented as #cachedBody('text') followed by JSON.parse.

hono.question: If a sub-app has its own app.notFound() and onError(), and is mounted with parent.route('/x', sub), which handlers apply to requests under /x?

hono.question: `throw new HTTPException(401, { res: new Response('nope', { status: 403 }) })`: what status does the client get?

Without res, the response body is the exception's message, and the status defaults to 500 when no status is given.

hono.question: How is the npm package built?
hono.reference: `bun run build` removes dist and runs `bun ./build/build.ts`. That script first checks that the package.json and jsr.json exports match, then globs src/**/*.ts as entry points, excluding tests, src/mod.ts, src/middleware.ts and src/deno/**. It runs three steps in parallel: an esbuild ESM build to dist with bundle: true and an add-extension plugin that keeps imports external and rewrites them to '.js', an esbuild CJS build to dist/cjs, and tsc --emitDeclarationOnly with tsconfig.build.json. Afterwards it strips #private fields from the .d.ts files. Then copy:package.cjs.json writes {"type":"commonjs"} into dist/cjs and dist/types, and the postbuild step runs publint.
